subject: Renewal proposal and SOW for SpendOptic (FinOps) - pricing clarification
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@spendoptic.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales_ops@spendoptic.com
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SpendOptic renewal: SOW + proposed pricing (Acme Analytics)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the time last week. Attached are the SOW (v3) and the pricing workbook that reflect the usage profile you shared for Acme Analytics. Highlights: a 12-month renewal with 15% platform discount, tiered overage bands, and a one-time onboarding credit to cover the migration of historical billing data.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm the start date (target: 2026-06-01).
- Confirm whether Acme will use the enterprise support add-on (we included it as optional).

I can loop in contracts if you want us to prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Attachments:
- SpendOptic_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, redlines in-line)
- SpendOptic_pricing_2026.xlsx (detailed rates and projections)

Best,
Olivia Chen
Senior Account Exec | SpendOptic
olivia@spendoptic.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 10:04:12 -0700
Subject: RE: SpendOptic renewal: SOW + proposed pricing (Acme Analytics)

Marcus / Laura — forwarding SpendOptic's renewal packet for Acme (attached). Short checklist:

1) Marcus — can you validate the usage bands vs our Q1 export (I attached a quick analysis). Does the proposed tiering map to our actual token/ingest distribution?
2) Laura — procurement will need standard terms; can you flag any clauses that need legal or security review (data retention / audit logs)?
3) I want to keep the onboarding credit, but need confirmation on support add-on. If Acme wants 24x7 it will change budget.

I propose we target an internal decision by next Tue so we can hit a 2026-06-01 start. Thoughts?

Mina
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 08:37:25 -0700
Subject: RE: SpendOptic renewal: SOW + proposed pricing (Acme Analytics)

Thanks Mina — quick read-through: the pricing tiers match the pattern but their baseline seems ~12% higher than our Q1 shipments. I ran the attached redwood_spend_analysis_Q1_2026.xlsx against their model and the delta looks driven by the 'ingest' multiplier and the overage band thresholds.

Proposed counterpoints for negotiation:
- Reduce baseline ingest multiplier by 10% (to reflect dedup improvements we've shipped).
- Keep the 12-month term but add an early renewal credit if Acme commits to a 24-month option.
- Push for a data-retention SLA addendum limiting historical retention to 90 days unless otherwise requested.

I'll mark up the pricing sheet and return to Olivia with specific numbers. If procurement needs an alternate PO structure (monthly vs annual), flag it and I'll include both options.

Marcus
FinOps Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@spendoptic.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, sales_ops@spendoptic.com
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 11:09:08 -0700
Subject: RE: SpendOptic renewal: SOW + proposed pricing (Acme Analytics)

Hi Mina / Marcus — thanks for the quick review. Short answers: we can reduce the ingest multiplier by 8% (we have limited flexibility on list pricing but can make customer-specific concessions), and we can add an SLA addendum for data retention (90 days by default).

Our proposal if Acme goes 24 months: additional 5% term discount applied to the platform fee and waiving the first-month overage. I'll attach a marked-up pricing workbook with these two scenarios.

DocuSign: I can prepare a DocuSign packet once you confirm the scenario (12mo baseline vs 24mo incentive). Also including a procurement mailbox for us: contracts@spendoptic.com

Best,
Olivia

-----Original Message-----

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:22:33 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme - recommendation and next steps

Team — after Marcus's markup and Olivia's concessions, my recommendation for Acme is: accept the 24-month deal with the 5% term discount and onboarding credit. Rationale: predictable revenue and lower unit price over time; Acme prefers longer term for budgeting.

Open items for procurement/legal before DocuSign:
- Laura: confirm if the SLA/data-retention addendum is standard or requires legal review (I suspect standard).
- Procurement: need PO template and whether Acme prefers annual invoices or a single annual invoice.
- Finance: need to confirm budget cadence, but Acme's finance contact (Samir) indicated approval pending our final SOW.

If there are no legal flags, I'm happy to ask Olivia to generate the DocuSign with the 24mo option. Please reply by EOD Wed 2026-04-28.

Mina

-----Original Message-----

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Internal: Acme - recommendation and next steps

Mina — quick confirmation: I reviewed the SOW and the SLA addendum. The data-retention clause as proposed (90 days by default, with exceptions handled by written request) is acceptable. No material legal redlines. Procurement note: Acme typically prefers an annual invoice; I'll include our PO template and ask them to confirm.

Approve moving to DocuSign for the 24-month option.
